_source: en-gb glossary; en_GB is a spelling-variant locale rather than a translation target
_note: Deliberately the emptiest config. en_GB is English, so most of these rules are Romance-language conventions that are simply wrong here: English DOES use Title Case in UI, DOES capitalise month names, DOES use '&', and DOES legitimately use a 12-hour am/pm clock. The real work for this locale is the glossary (British spelling) plus the locale-neutral checks.

6e_apostrophe_accent._why: not-applicable: English has no accented vowels to mistype.

6f_title_case._why: not-applicable: English UI legitimately uses Title Case for labels and buttons.

6g_space_before_punctuation._why: English attaches punctuation to the preceding word.

6g_oxford_comma._why: not-applicable: the Oxford comma is a legitimate and widely used English style, not an error.

6h_ampersand._why: not-applicable: '&' is normal in English UI copy.

6i_loanword_plural._why: not-applicable: these are English words in English; the -s plural is correct.

6j_please._why: not-applicable: the source string's own 'Please' is being preserved, not humanised.

6k_gerund._why: not-applicable: the English gerund stays a gerund.

6l_clock_24h._why: not-applicable: en_GB legitimately uses 12-hour am/pm as well as 24-hour.
